llm.summary: The instructions describe a powerful auto-updater that reads user configs and restarts the gateway, but the skill package includes no script/install, declares no required binaries or config paths, and mixes Windows/cron semantics — the pieces don't line up.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be an OpenClaw auto-updater (updates core and skills, restarts gateway) which legitimately requires access to configs, npm, and the clawhub CLI — but the registry metadata lists no required binaries, no config paths, and no primary credential. That mismatch (metadata shows nothing required while the instructions require PowerShell, npm, and clawhub and access to ~/.openclaw/* files) is inconsistent and unexplained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/operator to run scripts/self-updater.ps1 and to read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json, perform npm and clawhub updates, and restart the gateway. Reading those config files and performing updates/restarts is in-scope for an updater, but the skill bundle does not include the referenced PowerShell script or declare that it will access those paths — that's scope creep/unrealized dependency. Also the doc mixes Windows-specific idle detection with cron/Linux scheduling examples, which is ambiguous and risky.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files (instruction-only). That is lower install risk, but also means the SKILL.md expects an external script (scripts/self-updater.ps1) and external CLIs to already exist. The absence of an included script or an install mechanism to fetch a vetted script is a notable omission: the agent or user would have to obtain/execute an external script from an unspecified source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or credentials, yet the runtime instructions require reading user configuration files (~/.openclaw/*), running networked update commands (npm, clawhub), and restarting a gateway — actions that can have broad effects. The lack of declared config paths and required binaries in metadata is inconsistent with the file and command access described in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good), and the skill is not force-installed. However, the updater is expected to restart the gateway and run system-level update commands (npm -g, clawhub update --all). Those are privileged actions relative to a typical skill and should be explicitly declared and permissioned. The skill does not declare that it will require elevated privileges, nor does it include safe-guarding guidance in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not enable/install this skill until you confirm its source and review the actual updater script. The SKILL.md references scripts/self-updater.ps1 and reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json, but the package contains no script or install instructions — that means you'd be relying on an external script whose origin is unknown. Before running: (1) obtain the updater script from a trusted source and inspect its contents, (2) verify whether npm and clawhub are needed and what permissions they require, (3) confirm which platform(s) are supported (the doc mixes Windows idle-API usage with cron examples), (4) run a dry-run in an isolated/test environment and back up OpenClaw configuration and data, (5) ensure you understand and accept that the updater may restart the gateway and perform global npm/clawhub updates. If you cannot review the script/code, treat this skill as untrusted.
